mapping_targets.structural_comparison: THE DMI uses a matrix of 4 pillars x 5 dimensions = 20 child dimensions with 4 maturity levels. QS uses 4 pillars > 14 categories > 33 sub-indicators with 3 capability levels. THE measures digital maturity broadly; QS measures AI capability specifically. An institution can score high on THE (good digital maturity) but low on QS (digital maturity has not been applied to AI specifically).

level_alignment.qs_basic: Closest to THE Incidental. Both describe ad-hoc, uncoordinated states.
level_alignment.qs_developing: Spans THE Intentional and early Integrated. QS Developing covers the range from purposeful action through to partial implementation.
level_alignment.qs_advanced: Closest to THE Integrated with elements of Optimised. QS does not have a separate Optimised level.

mappings.what_transfers: Institutional governance structures, strategic planning approaches, leadership accountability patterns.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: QS governance is AI-specific (AI risk, AI ethics, AI procurement). THE governance covers all digital transformation. An institution with strong digital governance may still lack AI-specific governance.
mappings.notes: This is a partial overlap. THE PG-Strategy and PG-People map loosely to QS Leadership & Capability. THE PG-Data maps loosely to QS Code of Conduct & Privacy. THE has no equivalent to QS Regulatory & Ethical Standards at the AI-specific level.

mappings.what_transfers: A strong AI regulatory compliance function implies strategic governance capability.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: THE Strategy covers all digital strategy. QS Regulatory is AI-specific. Strong THE Strategy does not imply AI regulatory compliance.
mappings.notes: QS Regulatory has no direct THE equivalent. It is an AI-specific concern that does not exist in general digital maturity.

mappings.what_transfers: Leadership commitment, workforce development approaches, cultural change management.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: QS Leadership is AI-specific leadership and AI training. THE People covers all digital skills and culture. AI leadership is a subset.
mappings.notes: QS Training & Development maps more closely to THE People & Culture than other QS governance categories.

mappings.what_transfers: Teaching innovation approaches, learning analytics maturity, assessment design, student experience focus.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: QS is AI-specific teaching capability. THE covers all digital teaching. An institution with excellent digital teaching may not have AI-specific teaching capability.
mappings.notes: This is the strongest pillar-level mapping. Both frameworks assess how technology is used in teaching, but at different specificity levels.

mappings.what_transfers: Strategic approach to technology in curriculum, programme review processes.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: QS Curriculum focuses on AI integration specifically. THE Strategy covers all digital teaching strategy.
mappings.notes: QS AI Literacy (3.1.3) has no direct THE equivalent. It is an AI-specific competency.

mappings.what_transfers: Technology adoption in assessment, feedback mechanisms.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: QS Assessment addresses AI-specific concerns (bias validation, adaptive assessment, AI-resilient design) that THE Utilisation does not cover.
mappings.notes: QS Bias Validation (3.3.3) is an AI-specific concern with no THE equivalent.

mappings.what_transfers: Research infrastructure approaches, data management maturity, research collaboration patterns.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: QS Research distinguishes between AI as a tool, AI as a subject of study, and AI as a research field. THE Research treats research technology holistically. QS Scholarship of AI (4.2) and AI Research (4.3) have no THE equivalent.
mappings.notes: QS has more granular research categories. THE Research is broader but less AI-specific.

mappings.what_transfers: Administrative efficiency, student support services, operational technology adoption.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: QS Outreach includes recruitment, external engagement, and industry partnerships. THE Professional Services covers IT, library, HR, finance, estates. The overlap is in operational efficiency and student services.
mappings.notes: QS External Engagement (2.4) has limited THE equivalent. THE does not have an outreach or partnership dimension.

mappings.what_transfers: Nothing. This is an AI-specific concern.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: AI sustainability impact is not covered in THE DMI.
mappings.notes: AI environmental impact is a distinctive QS concern reflecting the framework's 2024 origins when AI compute costs became a sector issue.

mappings.what_transfers: Nothing. AI literacy is a specific competency not covered by THE's digital skills dimension.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: THE People & Culture covers general digital skills but not AI literacy as a distinct competency.
mappings.notes: AI literacy as a graduate attribute and institutional competency is a QS-specific concern.

mapping_targets.mapping_type: AI-specific institutional to AI-specific institutional (closest structural peer)
mapping_targets.structural_comparison: JISC AI Maturity uses 5 progressive stages (Approaching, Experimenting, Operational, Embedded, Optimised) across themes (strategic adoption, students/learners, supporting staff, academic integrity, safe/responsible use). QS uses 4 pillars > 14 categories > 33 sub-indicators with 3 capability levels. JISC is journey-oriented (what institutions do at each stage). QS is capability-oriented (what institutions can do). Both are AI-specific institutional frameworks, making this the highest-value mapping pair.

level_alignment.qs_basic: Maps to JISC Stage 1 (Approaching and Understanding). Both describe early, uncoordinated states.
level_alignment.qs_developing: Maps to JISC Stages 2-3 (Experimenting and Exploring / Operational). QS Developing spans a wider range than any single JISC stage.
level_alignment.qs_advanced: Maps to JISC Stages 4-5 (Embedded / Optimised). QS Advanced combines what JISC splits into two stages.

mappings.what_transfers: Ethical AI use, regulatory compliance, responsible deployment.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: QS separates regulatory compliance from ethical guidelines from sustainability impact. JISC combines these under safe/responsible use.
mappings.notes: QS is more granular in governance. JISC provides more detailed stage descriptions.

mappings.what_transfers: Governance structures, institutional decision-making, risk management.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: JISC Strategic Adoption is broader than QS Risk Management. QS Risk is more specific about AI risk assessment processes.
mappings.notes: Many-to-many mapping. QS governance categories collectively map to JISC Strategic Adoption.

mappings.what_transfers: Staff development, training, capability building.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: QS Leadership includes strategic planning and senior accountability. JISC Supporting Staff focuses on workforce development. These are related but different.
mappings.notes: QS Leadership & Planning (1.4.1) maps to JISC Strategic Adoption. QS Training & Development (1.4.2) maps to JISC Supporting Staff.

mappings.what_transfers: AI in curriculum, student AI literacy, learning experience.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: QS Curriculum focuses on institutional curriculum design. JISC Students/Learners focuses on learner experience and outcomes.
mappings.notes: QS AI Literacy maps well to JISC's emphasis on student AI capability.

mappings.what_transfers: AI assessment approaches, integrity management, AI-resilient assessment design.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: QS Assessment is broader (includes feedback and adaptive assessment). JISC Academic Integrity is narrower but deeper on integrity specifically.
mappings.notes: The closest category-level mapping in the two frameworks.

mappings.what_transfers: Nothing directly. JISC does not have a research pillar.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: QS Research & Scholarship (AI tools for research, AI scholarship, AI research) has no JISC equivalent. JISC focuses on teaching and institutional operations.
mappings.notes: This is the most significant structural gap between the two frameworks. JISC's focus on teaching and operations means research AI capability is not assessed.

mappings.what_transfers: Some operational AI adoption practices.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: QS Outreach covers recruitment, career services, administrative efficiency, and external partnerships. JISC has no equivalent operational AI pillar.
mappings.notes: This is a weak mapping. QS Outreach is distinctive and largely unmapped in JISC.

mapping_targets.target_framework_name: UNESCO Guidance on AI and Education
mapping_targets.structural_comparison: UNESCO provides policy guidance for governments and institutions on AI in education. It is not a maturity or capability framework but a set of principles and recommendations. The mapping identifies where QS institutional capability aligns with UNESCO policy recommendations.

level_alignment.note: UNESCO does not use maturity levels. The mapping identifies alignment between QS capability areas and UNESCO policy themes.

mappings.what_transfers: UNESCO principles on ethical AI use inform what QS Regulatory capability should achieve.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: UNESCO provides principles. QS measures institutional capability to implement them. Knowing the principles does not constitute capability.
mappings.notes: UNESCO's ethical AI principles provide the 'what' that QS's Regulatory category operationalises as the 'how'.

mappings.what_transfers: UNESCO data protection principles directly inform QS data protection capability requirements.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: UNESCO is guidance. QS is capability measurement.
mappings.notes: Strong conceptual alignment.

mappings.unesco_element_name: AI Competencies for Students and Teachers
mappings.what_transfers: UNESCO's recommendations on AI literacy and competencies inform QS curriculum expectations.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: UNESCO defines what competencies are needed. QS measures whether the institution builds them.
mappings.notes: UNESCO AI Competency Framework (2024) is the most specific related document.

mappings.unesco_element_name: Inclusive and Equitable AI in Education
mappings.what_transfers: UNESCO emphasis on equity in AI education informs how QS personalisation should be evaluated (not just personalised, but equitably personalised).
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: UNESCO's equity focus is broader than educational personalisation.
mappings.notes: QS Bias Validation (3.3.3) directly reflects UNESCO equity principles.

mappings.what_transfers: UNESCO's emphasis on AI for sustainable development aligns with QS's sustainability impact indicator.
mappings.what_does_not_transfer: UNESCO focuses on AI as a tool for SDGs. QS focuses on the environmental sustainability of AI itself.
mappings.notes: Related but different angles on AI and sustainability.
